newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus Lombard NatWest offers private banking.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus Lombard NatWest offers private banking.

text.p: Cyprus-based Lombard NatWest on Monday announced the launch of private banking services in cooperation with Coutts Zurich.
The bank is offering four types of managed fund accounts (MFA's) with a varying degree of risk which will invest in Coutts funds and third party funds.

Clients can select from an MFA which invests only in bond or money market funds, those which invest in bond and money markets with limited exposure to equities, a fund which invests equally in bonds, money markets and equities and one that invests primarily in equity funds.

"The MFA provides the investor with a number of additional key benefits, namely the potential for higher returns than cash deposits in the longer term, a high level of diversification and thus reduction or risk, direct access to all of the world's major financial markets, professional portfolio management and relatively low transaction costs and management fees," said Popi Hadjioannou, the Private Banking Officer at Lombard NatWest.
The MFAs are available in dollars, sterling, the mark and the Swiss franc. The minimum investment is $100,000.

The service is offered to investors who are allowed to hold foreign currency assets under current legislation. This category includes offshore companies, non residents and expatriates, and Cypriot Insurance and Investment Funds which are allowed to invest up to 20 percent of their funds abroad.
Bank officials said an increasing number of Cypriot individuals would be able to invest in managed fund accounts and private banking services after the pending liberalisation of capital flows.
National Westminster Bank owns 75 percent of Lombard NatWest in Cyprus. -- Nicosia newsroom 357 2 365089
